headline: Highest risk is medium: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate document contents via broad network/MCP, while marker is local-only and read/write constrained, limiting direct injection and conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem read/write, shell, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. B can use browsers and MCP, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel; only manual copy-paste or external bridging is plausible. That makes prompt injection possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B’s generated text into A’s prompt or workflow, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP server or clipboard bridge is added, B’s content can influence A.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted B output into A workflows.
Use a fixed prompt template for A with no free-form pasted instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared text bridge.
requires-engineering: isolate B’s browser/MCP outputs from A inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and has broad network egress plus API integrations, so document contents can leave the local workspace. A is local-only and touches no data classes, so it does not add leakage surface. The pair is risky because B can transmit shared document contents to third-party services by default.
conditions: IF B processes sensitive PDFs, images, or diagram XML, those contents may be sent to external model APIs.
IF A is used to pre-process documents that are then handed to B, the same data can flow onward through B's networked calls.
mitigations: Route sensitive documents only to local/offline workflows.
Disable external API providers in B for sensitive jobs.
Review and restrict B’s allowed file types before processing.
Use a separate workspace for non-sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and redaction before API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B supports multiple instances and broad network use, but without A write access there is no meaningful shared-write conflict. The only overlap is read-side document handling, which is not a capability conflict.
conditions: IF A is replaced with a version that can write the same workspace as B, write conflicts could emerge.
IF B is configured to mutate shared files while another writer is introduced, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Assign B a separate output directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same diagram files.
requires-engineering: add file locking for shared mutable workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s natural-language visualization workflow can treat upstream text as authoritative, and A is a document processor whose outputs may be fed into B. Because A has no verification or action-taking authority, the cascade is limited to incorrect diagrams or summaries rather than external actions, but the default handoff still creates an unverified dependency.
conditions: IF A’s extracted text is pasted into B without human review, B may render or act on incorrect facts.
IF B is used to generate diagrams from A’s output, errors can propagate into downstream work products.
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A output.
Compare A output against the source document for key facts.
Use a checklist for diagram labels and entities.
Limit B to draft-only outputs until verified.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles files and API keys and can send content to multiple external providers, creating residency and retention uncertainty for document data. A is open-source and local-only with no data classes touched, so it is not the main compliance driver. The pair therefore inherits B’s external-processing compliance burden, especially for regulated documents.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through B’s external APIs, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF B is configured with a non-compliant provider for the document class, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Restrict B to compliant providers only.
Do not process regulated documents through external APIs.
Document retention and deletion settings for each provider.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workloads.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class and region.
